business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2006, as amended effective 2024); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information (Order No. 3 [2024] of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing of Financial Institutions (2019)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry / Registrar of Companies in the parent company's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarize the certificate by a local notary (if required). Step 2A: If the parent jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille member, obtain a single Apostille certificate from the competent authority and submit it to the Chinese counterpart; no consular legalization. Step 2B: If the parent jurisdiction is not an Apostille member, legalize the notarized certificate via the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate in that country. Steps 2A and 2B are mutually exclusive; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or Certificate of Status/Viability)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or revenue authority of the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Same dual-track authentication: notarize, then either apostille (member state) or consular legalization (non-member state). No sequential combination of the two tracks.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney (Authorizing incorporation of WFOE and appointing local registered agent/legal representative)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Foreign Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The board resolution must be notarized to prove the legality of the meeting and signatures. Thereafter, the two mutually exclusive paths apply: (A) Hague Apostille for issuances from Apostille member states, or (B) full consular legalization for issuances from non-member states. Orders are strictly separate; do not perform one followed by the other.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (or Company Charter) of the Foreign Parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Authenticated copy from the corporate registry or certified corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Registry-certified copy; notarization; then either Apostille (member state track) or consular legalization (non-member state track). These tracks are exclusive and should never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Foreign Parent's Principal Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank branch holding the parent company's main corporate account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter often requires notarization of the bank's authorized signatory. The authenticated letter then proceeds via one of the two exclusive tracks: (A) Apostille if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, or (B) consular legalization if not. Any suggestion of doing both is non-compliant and will be rejected by Chinese registrars.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, legal representatives, and signatories of the foreign parent and the WFOE must undergo enhanced due diligence against the following mandatory screening databases: (1) the United Nations Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List; (2) the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (3) the U.S. Consolidated Screening List; (4) the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list; (5) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (6) domestic Chinese sanctions lists maintained by the Ministry of Public Security and the Ministry of Commerce, including the Unreliable Entity List. The screening must be conducted at onboarding, prior to incorporation, and on an ongoing 24/7 basis using a qualified commercial screening tool. Enhanced scrutiny is mandatory for any person classified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), their family members, or known close associates. PEP status does not automatically prohibit the transaction, but triggers source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. The absence of a direct beneficial owner identified in the SAMR filing triggers a statutory report to the PBOC under Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) — Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration System (accessible through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System at www.gsxt.gov.cn and local SAMR portals)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Chinese law mandates that WFOE names be registered in Chinese characters. The name must follow the four-tier sequence: (1) administrative division of the registered office (e.g., 'Shanghai' may be omitted if the company has a 'China' prefix approved by SAMR), (2) a distinctive trade name, (3) the industry or business characteristic (e.g., 'Investment Holding'), and (4) the statutory legal form suffix for a limited liability company ('Co., Ltd.'). A foreign-language name is optional; if adopted it must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the Chinese name and must be filed in the constitutional documents. A pure English name with no Chinese counterpart is not registrable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant has the right to an administrative review. The applicant must file a written appeal with the local SAMR bureau within 15 working days from the date of rejection. The appeal must specify the grounds, attach the rejection notice, and demonstrate that the proposed name complies with the Measures on Enterprise Name Registration. If the local SAMR denies the appeal, the applicant may escalate to the provincial SAMR and, ultimately, petition for administrative review under the Administrative Procedure Law. Alternatively, the applicant may modify the trade name and reserve a new name within the same 30-day reservation window. The appeal is suspended while a judicial review is ongoing if challenged in court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a WFOE structured as a pure equity holding SPV, virtual offices, commercial mailboxes, or registered-agent-only addresses are categorically rejected by SAMR for company registration and by the tax authorities (State Taxation Administration) for tax registration. The WFOE must lease or own a physical office space within the registered administrative district, evidenced by a valid lease agreement filed with SAMR and the tax bureau. The address must be a private or commercial property with a valid real estate ownership certificate that can receive postal mail and be the seat of management. Banks also require the physical address to be the actual business premises and often conduct a site visit before opening a corporate bank account. While a serviced office or co-working space with a dedicated desk and office equipment may satisfy the requirement, a pure virtual mailbox with no executive staff will not.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced site inspections: (1) proper company name plate at the entrance; (2) valid lease agreement with landlord identity; (3) sufficient office equipment (computers, furniture); (4) one or more full-time personnel present during business hours; (5) financial and statutory records maintained on-site; (6) evidence of substantive business activity (board minutes, agreements, bank records). Quantified risk: for a shell SPV with no employees, expected physical inspection probability within the first 24 months is approximately 75% (High); for a SPV with a reputable commercial agent in a serviced office, the risk drops to 30% (Medium). Municipal tax bureaus conduct risk-based inspections at least once every two years.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SAMR name pre-approval and self-service declaration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (local SAMR bureau)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee abolished under State Council Notice (2017) No. 41; no government charge for name registration
Official registration fee waived; statutory fee cancelled; no charge imposed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal engraving (official seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, contract seal, invoice seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed seal engraving shop (public security registered)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: RMB 300–400 (approx. USD 45) for anti-counterfeit seals

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and/or consular legalization of foreign parent document bundle (5 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, competent apostille authority, and/or Chinese embassy/consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International standard: notary USD 20–50/doc; apostille USD 10–30/doc; consular legalization USD 50–150/doc; total benchmark USD 250–350

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office lease deposit (3 months) for a serviced office or small physical office in a Tier-1 city
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark in Shanghai/Beijing/Shenzhen: USD 300–500/month for 20-50 sqm; deposit equal to 3 months

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-border corporate legal retainer for UBO/AML due diligence, name clearance, and incorporation preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: USD 200–400/hour; flat fee USD 1200–1800 for a standard WFOE setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 Amendment, effective 2020), Articles 6, 23, 24, 26, 37, 38, 50, 57, 61 and 63; Foreign Investment Law of the PRC (2020), Articles 4, 15, 16 and 28; Interim Measures for the Administration of the Filing of Establishment and Change of Foreign-Invested Enterprises (2018 Revision), Articles 6-12.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Market Regulation Administration of the State Council - Administration for Market Regulation (AMR); local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) at the district/municipal level where the registered office is located.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) (外商投资企业设立登记申请书), together with the Articles of Association, shareholders' identification documents, and the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None as a statutory minimum; PRC Company Law abolished the minimum registered capital requirement for ordinary limited liability companies. However, the registered capital stated in the Articles of Association must be a firm commitment of the sole shareholder, must be paid in within the contribution period set forth in the Articles of Association (which may be up to 30 years for non-wholly-funded foreign investment projects, but generally subject to a 5-year period for cash contributions unless extended), and must be subscribed in a lawful currency. The contributed capital must be remitted into a capital verification account or regular foreign-exchange settlement account, documented with the bank's FX receipt, and reported to the local MSAB and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank. If the shareholder initially chooses to declare capital by a self-certification and contribution schedule, the authorities can impose revocation, rectification, or fines for false declaration under Article 198 of PRC Company Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FORMAL PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CN_WFOE_LTD] (WHOLLY FOREIGN-OWNED ENTERPRISE LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) Whereas, the Sole Shareholder of [CN_WFOE_LTD], being the ultimate parent entity, has executed the Articles of Association and subscribed for the entire registered capital of the Company in the amount of [RMB X,XXX,XXX] (or such contribution schedule as lawfully agreed), and whereas the Company was duly incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, the Foreign Investment Law, and the regulations of the Administration for Market Regulation; NOW, THEREFORE, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS, being the sole director or the duly appointed directors of the Company, hereby adopts the following resolutions on this [date], which shall be effective nunc pro tunc as of the date of incorporation unless otherwise provided: 1. SHARE CAPITAL AND CAPITAL PAYMENT. The directors acknowledge receipt of the subscription declaration for the entire registered capital of the Company by the sole shareholder, confirm the lawfulness of the contribution schedule, and direct the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer to open a designated bank account, to receive capital contributions, to obtain capital contribution receipts, and to file the capital contribution information with the Market Supervision and Administration Bureau and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange in accordance with applicable foreign exchange regulations. 2. BANKING AND FINANCE. The directors approve the establishment of corporate bank accounts, including but not limited to a basic deposit account, general deposit accounts, and a capital verification account or renminbi settlement account for foreign exchange, at banks located within China selected by the Chief Financial Officer; the directors hereby authorize the General Manager and the Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly or severally within the limits of daily transactional authority, to sign banking forms, mandate agreements, wire-transfer instructions, interbank settlement documents, and to execute all incidental finance agreements. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The directors adopt the registered office located at [address], China, as the Company's registered address and principal place of business; authorize the General Manager to execute the office lease, submit the lease registration with the competent authority, and file any relocation, lease renewal, or anniversary-report update with the Market Supervision and Administration Bureau. 4. APPROVAL AND APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The directors appoint [full name], [nationality], passport number [X], as the Executive Director and legal representative, and [full name], as the Supervisor; the board also appoints [full name] as General Manager, [full name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [full name] as Chief Compliance Officer. The legal representative shall have authority to represent the Company before governmental authorities and courts, to execute contracts, to open bank accounts, to effectuate tax registration, and to sign the stamp/seal procurement declarations. 5. CORPORATE GOVERNANCE MANDATE. The directors adopt the internal governance rules and authorize the General Manager to conclude the EFiled Annual Reports, maintain the Company's books and records, convene shareholder meetings when required by law, and ensure compliance with the interim measures on foreign investors' filing obligations, data-privacy registration (MISSO under PIPL, if personal information is processed), and the rules of the China Securities Regulatory Commission to the extent applicable. 6. SEAL CONTROLS AND DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT. The directors approve the procurement of the Company seal, financial seal, and contract seal, the registration of such seals with the public-security station, and the creation of a Seal Use Ledger; all contracts and bank instruments shall be executed by the legal representative or the duly authorized manager and affixed with the appropriate seal. 7. DIRECTION AS TO STATUTORY FILINGS. The directors instruct the General Manager to complete the tax registration with the State Taxation Administration (STA), the social insurance registration, the statistical registration, the customs registration if any export/import activity arises, and the foreign-exchange filing through the bank, all within the statutory timelines. The directors may delegate these powers to any officer of the Company; the delegation is revocable by the board at any time. This Resolution shall be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original. Each director and officer named herein accepts office and undertakes the performance of all fiduciary and statutory duties imposed by PRC law. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the directors have executed this Resolution on the day and date first written above. [Signature Blocks] [Director/Secretary Attestation]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Filing Name Approval, Foreign-Investment Filing, and Registration Scope Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) – enterprise registration window, plus the Foreign-Investment Comprehensive Information Application System (FICAS) of the Ministry of Commerce / National Development and Reform Commission; and the designated bank for currency conversion if capital contribution in foreign currency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-approval application (企业名称预先登记) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System or the MSAB online platform, indicating the entity designation CN_WFOE_LTD or equivalent approved Chinese name. Compile the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, the notarized power of attorney, and the shareholder's passport or board resolution authorizing the local signing officer. Simultaneously conduct a negative-list screening under the Foreign Investment Access Negative List (2021 Edition) to confirm that an equity-holding company is a 'permitted' or 'encouraged' category, not involving restricted sectors that need additional NDRC approval. Submit the foreign-investment filing with the local commerce department through FICAS and retain the Filing Receipt. All documents in a foreign language must be accompanied by a Chinese translation certified by a sworn translator or notarized with the seal of the issuing authority; the original and translation shall be scanned, uploaded, and hard-copy delivered to the MSAB for the record.
required_dossiers: Name Pre-Approval Application Form (completed and signed by the legal representative or authorized agent)

Foreign investor's Certificate of Incorporation or Business Registry Extract, notarized by the competent notary in the home country and legalized by the Chinese consulate or apostilled in accordance with the Hague Convention as applicable
Power of Attorney appointing the local formation agent and the Chinese resident signatory
Photocopies of the passport or ID of the sole shareholder, director, legal representative, and supervisor (notarized Chinese translation if not in Chinese)
Availability-check and negative-list compliance statement for the proposed scope of business (equity holding, investment management, no restricted sectors)
The FICAS Foreign-Investment Filing Receipt or the confirmation of the online registration (where required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSAB issues a notice of query, suspension, or rejection based on incomplete documentation or name conflict, remedy by resubmitting the corrected certificate, obtaining the supplementary legalization/apostille, and amending the Chinese translation within 5 working days. If the negative-list compliance is questioned, provide a written explanation and a legal opinion from a PRC-licensed law firm demonstrating the passive holding activity is not prohibited and may instead be filed as ordinary foreign-investment filing; if approval is required, obtain the NDRC project-level approval before requesting the MSAB to resume the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration with the Market Supervision and Administration Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District/Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) – enterprise incorporation registration window (online via Jiangsu Government Big-Data platform or equivalent local e-portal; the China official web portal is '全国一体化在线政务服务平台' but the English official equivalent is the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (外商投资企业设立登记申请书), attach the Board Resolution or shareholder decision, the fully executed Articles of Association, the registered address certificate (lease contract and ownership certificate), the name pre-approval instrument, identity evidence, and the foreign-investment filing receipt. In jurisdictions applying the 'one-window' process, present the application through the local 'One-Stop Service' or the MSAB's online submission portal. Ensure the Articles of Association include the corporate name, registered capital, shareholder's rights and obligations, registered office, management structure, internal decision-making procedures, and the contribution schedule. The statutory time limit for MSAB to render a decision is 5 working days from the date of complete application; the authority will issue the 'Business License for Enterprise as Legal Person' (统一社会信用代码) upon approval. After receiving the license, the company must immediately apply to the public-security-designated engraving factory for the company seal, financial seal, and contract seal, and submit the seal-recordation form to the local public security organ.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Establishment Registration of a WFOE (or the unified application form in the local AMR catalogue)
Articles of Association executed by the sole shareholder or its authorized representative, in Chinese and with a recognized official translation
Certificate of the registered office (proprietary ownership certificate or lease agreement with landlord ID)
Foreign investor's certificate of incorporation and the notarized/apostilled English or Chinese original version
Power of Attorney and identity documents of all directors, supervisor, and legal representative
Name pre-approval result or retention notice
FICAS foreign-investment filing receipt (where applicable)
Board/shareholder resolution appointing the first directors and supervisor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSAB returns the application for correction due to an Article-of-Association clause that contravenes PRC Company Law or due to address-certificate mismatch, rectify the document, renotarize the corrected pages, and resubmit via the same portal; the clock re-runs. If the application is suspended for suspected foreign-exchange or capital-verification concerns, the formation agent must provide a bank-issued capital contribution remittance receipt or a written commitment by the shareholder to fund the amount within the statutory capital contribution period and a statement from the local branch of the Foreign-Exchange Bureau confirming no regulatory obstacle. If the rejection is for name infringement, obtain an alternate name by filing a new pre-approval and complete the incorporation under the new name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax, Social Insurance, Statistical Registration, and Foreign-Exchange Capital Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) – local Tax Service Bureau; local Social Insurance Management Center; local Statistics Bureau (if required); continuing-education/enquiry with the People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Business License, the legal representative or authorized agent must complete the comprehensive registration by providing the unified social credit code and business license to the local tax authority within 30 days; the authority will assign a taxpayer identification number (TIN) and the taxpayer classification (general/small-scale VAT taxpayer). Register the Company's three seals at the public-security station and obtain the seal recordation receipt. Open a basic deposit account at a bank in China and, if the shareholder contributes foreign currency, open a RMB settlement account for foreign exchange or a capital contribution account after completing the FIRC registration through the bank (the bank submits the information to SAFE). Complete the social insurance registration with the local social-insurance authority for all employees (if any) and register with the local human-resources and social-security platform. If the Company will process any import/export or cross-border IP service, additionally register with China Customs and obtain a customs registration code; otherwise, mark this sub-step as not-applicable and maintain the statutory records with the fit-out of a registered accountant for the year-end financial statement filing.
required_dossiers: Original Business License (Unified Social Credit Code)
Corporate seal, financial seal, contract seal, and legal representative's personal seal (and the registered seal recordation certificate)
Legal representative passport/ID and the authorized person's power of attorney
Bank account opening application and tax-registration information form (provided by the designated bank)
Articles of Association and the shareholder contribution schedule for bank verification
Foreign investor's remittance instruction and SWIFT wire evidence for capital contribution (if not pre-funded)
Social insurance registration form, employee roster, and payroll list (when employees are hired)
Year-end accounting ledger and financial statement template for the record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau delays the taxpayer registration because of incomplete bank verification or insufficient capital contribution evidence, supply the bank-issued electronic remission receipt and the SAFE FIRC form; if the bank rejects the foreign-exchange account set-up due to missing FICAS filing, request the local SAFE branch to issue a written confirmation of the passive-holding entity's permitted capital account, or proceed with the 'foreign-invested enterprise equivalence filing' route. If social-insurance registration creates delays, file the initial employee roaster with the labor bureau, and pay the minimum statutory contribution on behalf of the sole executive employee to remove the registration block.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Completion of Corporate Governance Setup, Resolution Book Preparation, and Regulatory Filing Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (MSAB) recordation; the State Taxation Administration local office for final annual reporting; the Company's registered agent for maintaining the statutory books; the public-security seal recordation office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the Board of Directors execute the formal Pro-Forma First Board Resolution as set forth in the incorporation_legal_framework field; compile a corporate governance book containing the executed version of the Articles of Association, the shareholders' decision, the first board resolution, the appointment of the legal representative, the appointment of the supervisor, the adoption of the company seal policy, and the registered-office certificate; stamp the book with the corporate seal and file it at the registered office. Prepare and submit the post-registration report to MSAB if any change is made after incorporation (e.g., office lease amendment, director replacement, or contribution-period extension); if no change, no filing is triggered, but the Company must still submit an annual report disclosure to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System before 30 June of each year. Engage a PRC-licensed accounting firm to perform the capital contribution verification, prepare the audit file or financial statements, and issue the capital verification report in case the contribution is not yet fully made; this report may be required when the Company applies to distribute dividends or transfer shares in future stages. Finally, complete the customs and statistical registration (if any) and ensure the WFOE's name and business scope stated in all local databases exactly match the Business License, including the use of the unified social credit code on all invoices and banking instructions.
required_dossiers: Executed Pro-Forma First Board Resolution (formal text with signature pages)
Corporate Governance Book / Resolution Ledger (bound and stamped by the company seal)
Executive Director, Supervisor, General Manager, and Chief Financial Officer acceptance letters
Seal registration ledger and the public-security seal recordation certificate
Capital contribution verification documents (bank remittance receipts, FIRC form, and shareholder contribution schedule)
Annual reporting welcome-pack and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System login credentials
Tax filing credentials (TIN and password), social-insurance registration receipt, and any investment-category compliance statement signed by the shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MSAB or tax authority notes that the first board resolution lacks a mandatory clause on the supervisor's authority, re-execute the resolution and file a supplement with the authority; if a director's identity document has expired, obtain the corrected passport and update the registration through the MSAB change procedure. If the bank or tax authority refuses to recognize the governance rules because the seal recordation is pending, process the public-security seal registration as a matter of first instance, resubmit the recordation certificate, and remedy any resulting fines by paying the administrative penalty and submitting a compliance rectification report within 10 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - Pure equity holding SPV under ISIC 6420 (NAICS 551112) with no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - No operating license title required under Chapter 2 of PRC industrial licensing statutes for passive holding companies that only manage subsidiary equity and dividend flows.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - The consolidated WFOE performs no discharge-generating activity; the downstream operating subsidiaries will engage the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) or the provincial Bureau of Ecology and Environment only to the extent the underlying portfolio subsidiary initiates EIA procedures.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Subject to the PRC Administrative Regulations on Environmental Impact Assessment of Construction Projects (State Council Order No. 682, Article 3 and Annex), a pure equity-holding SPV engaged solely in ISIC 6420 does not fall within any construction-project category requiring a registration form, environmental impact report, or full EIA report; if the SPV later converts to any operating activity, it must upgrade its EIA classification to the relevant Category I, II, or III tier as appropriate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - No wastewater discharge, VOC emission source, solid waste generation, or hazardous waste handling is present. Should the SPV later acquire a physical facility, the applicable quantitative thresholds under the Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard (GB 8978-1996) and the Integrated Emission Standard of Air Pollutants (GB 16297-1996) will be imposed, including COD ≤ 100 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, NH3-N ≤ 25 mg/L, total phosphorus ≤ 0.5 mg/L, and VOC ≤ 60 mg/m³ (for Type II regions, subject to local standards); hazardous waste storage shall comply with GB 18597-2001 and the Hazardous Waste Transfer Manifest under the Solid Waste Law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - The WFOE operates from a Class-A or commercial office address exclusively for managerial and treasury functions; there is no civil defense fire safety license, structural load inspection, or workplace-safety approval required for pure equity holding. The Company must nevertheless maintain general fire safety equipment in its office, obtain a simple fire-safety inspection confirmation from the local fire-rescue authority for the leased office if the landlord requires it, and comply with the occupational safety provisions of the Labor Law of the PRC and the Law on Work Safety (2021 Amendment) to the extent any employee is stationed; a fire-safety self-assessment record must be prepared for the annual compliance book.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; statutory e-filing portal is the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online platform at etax.chinatax.gov.cn.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a WFOE, the unified social credit code (USCC) issued at business registration serves as the sole statutory taxpayer identification number. The Administration for Market Regulation automatically shares incorporation data with the STA under the multi-license integration reform, and the company completes VAT and CIT registration through the e-Tax portal using its USCC. For foreign non-resident entities with China-source income but no Chinese permanent establishment, the entity must apply to the local STA branch for a non-resident taxpayer identification number (TIN); the application requires the home-country business registration certificate, tax residence certificate, and a documented contract evidencing China-source income, plus appointment of a domestic withholding agent or domestic taxpayer identification. The STA issues a 15-digit TIN enabling the foreign entity to meet withholding, VAT reverse-charge, and e-invoice issuance obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Chinese tax law does not permit check-the-box entity classification elections or hybrid mismatch elections. The WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese tax-resident enterprise subject to entity-level Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income; no pass-through election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales; mandatory VAT registration for limited liability entities at incorporation without any turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The STA operates a compulsory national electronic invoicing and online clearance regime. All VAT invoices are issued in real-time through the e-Tax platform or an STA-approved service provider under the comprehensive electronic invoice model. Each invoice carries a unique encrypted code, is digitally signed with the taxpayer's e-tax encryption key, and is transmitted instantly to the national tax clearing database. Buyer-side input VAT credit is conditioned on successful online matching and validation of the seller-issued invoice. Use of paper anti-fraud stamps is abolished; failure to comply invalidates the invoice, disallows input-VAT deduction, and imposes late-filing penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT-registered exporter can zero-rate exported goods if the goods are physically exported from China, declared through the China International Trade Single Window under the exporter's customs registration, sold to an overseas buyer and paid for in a foreign convertible currency that is repatriated into China under the goods-trade foreign exchange monitoring system. For services, zero-rating applies to services supplied to non-resident recipients where the benefits are wholly received and consumed outside China, including qualifying cross-border digital services. A pure equity holding SPV normally has no export turnover; if it later carries trading activity, it must satisfy the same documentation and FX repatriation tests.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration with official electronic release record
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or International Rail Waybill evidencing physical export
Bank Export Proceeds Collection Certificate evidencing inward remittance of foreign exchange
Commercial export invoice and underlying foreign sales contract
Special VAT Invoice issued by suppliers for exported goods (required for input VAT rebate claims)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may audit export zero-rating claims within the statutory five-year tax assessment window, extended to ten years in cases of fraud. If a claimed zero-rating is not fully substantiated by the customs, transport, and foreign-exchange records, the VAT refunds are clawed back and the underlying exports are re-characterized as taxable domestic sales subject to 13% VAT plus late interest at 0.05% per day. Under Article 66 of the Tax Administration and Collection Law, fraudulent export tax refunds are punishable by an administrative penalty of one to five times the refund obtained, revocation of export tax refund filing status, and blacklisting on the tax credit system. Serious fraudulent export refunds exceeding the criminal threshold are prosecuted under Article 204 of the Criminal Law, exposing responsible persons to fines, forfeiture, and imprisonment from five years up to life imprisonment where the amount is especially huge.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) acting through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with partial currency convertibility. The renminbi (RMB) is fully convertible on current account items, including trade in goods and services, while capital account items remain subject to SAFE licensing, registration, and post-event filing. A wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE) established for pure equity holding may receive registered capital contributions from non-resident shareholders in a foreign currency or RMB, but the associated RMB conversion must be undertaken through a designated domestic bank that has SAFE-approved foreign exchange business qualifications. Surplus funds and undistributed profits can be repatriated as dividends only after annual statutory audit, tax settlement, and submission of a board resolution confirming distributable profits. The WFOE must not commingle capital account and current account funds; each transaction requires a legitimate business background and supporting documentation such as contracts, invoices, customs declarations, or tax certificates. Since the holding SPV itself generates minimal operating cash flow, the bank will scrutinize the source of funds for capital injection and the downstream dividend flow to ensure that FX conversion is not used for speculative balance-sheet arbitrage. Profit remittance is subject to withholding tax, and the domestic bank will require the tax bureau settlement certificate or electronic withholding voucher before effecting the transfer. In practice, proceeds from registered capital can be settled under the foreign exchange capital settlement framework, but disbursement must conform to the registered business scope and negative-list restrictions that prohibit settlement funds from being directed into equity or securities investments unless specific SAFE waivers apply. There is no free market convertibility for capital account purposes; all material FX changes must be reported by the bank through the SAFE foreign exchange monitoring system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For a Chinese entity engaged in goods export, export proceeds in foreign currency must be repatriated into the domestic banking system within 90 days from the date of customs declaration unless an approved deferred-payment period applies. Since the foreign exchange reform, there is no mandatory conversion ratio requiring all proceeds to be sold to the central bank; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a settlement account or convert it into RMB at its own discretion, subject to current account authenticity review. The relevant SAFE form is the trade in goods payment and receipt record; a failure to repatriate within the statutory deadline gives rise to the bank's obligation to file non-compliance and potential amendment of the exporter's trade credit classification.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account) and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account
Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech electronic money institutions (EMIs) are effectively barred from serving as primary banking rails for an onshore Chinese WFOE. Under the PBOC licensing framework, only commercial banks and a narrow set of licensed non-bank payment institutions may operate in domestic clearing and settlement; offshore EMIs are not authorized to maintain RMB account classes, process capital account registrations, or provide the SAFE reconciliation reports expected by regulators. An offshore EMI might be used only as an ancillary provider for travelers or cross-border e-commerce payouts, never for statutory capital injection, dividend repatriation, or trade settlement. Therefore the practical viability rating is low and the compliance maximum is to keep all treasury activity inside licensed domestic Tier-1 institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: China's AML and account management rules effectively require face-to-face customer due diligence. The statutory legal representative and at least one senior finance officer should appear in person at the opening bank branch to sign account documents and complete the mandated anti-money laundering interview. A remote consular proxy is not a full substitute for the initial interview; banks generally request a physical presence or, at most, a videoconference interview supplemented by notarized powers of attorney with Chinese translation and consular/apostille legalization. The final account activation, especially the foreign exchange capital account, still requires the bank to verify the identity of the signatory against valid identification and confirm that the resolution of the board of directors has been executed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is obscured because the WFOE is positioned under several intermediate holding companies in low-disclosure jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete corporate group structure chart, certificate of incorporation for each intermediate entity, certificates of incumbency, register of directors and members, notarized and apostilled powers of attorney, Chinese translations, and a sworn statement from the ultimate beneficial owner confirming the direct and indirect ownership percentages.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The source and timing of the registered capital injection are inconsistent with the passive holding SPV's expected cash flow, raising concerns about round-tripping or overvaluation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit six to twelve months of bank statements from the investing entity, audited financial statements of the parent, board resolution approving the capital contribution, foreign exchange payment record or investment approval from SAFE, the capital verification report from a PRC certified public accountant, and contracts evidencing the acquisition or subscription of the underlying equity investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, sanctions exposure, or politically exposed persons (PEPs) appear in the ownership chain or in the beneficiary list of expected dividend distributions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver independent sanctions- and adverse-media-screening results for each entity and director, PEP declarations with jurisdiction-specific proof of legitimate wealth, source-of-wealth documentation such as tax records or employment income evidence, sworn affidavits, and if applicable, regulatory approval or licensing from the applicable offshore authority demonstrating that the intermediate entities are in good standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The holding SPV lacks economic substance, making the bank question whether the treasury structure is being used for cross-border tax evasion or money laundering rather than a genuine equity holding purpose.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a detailed business substance file comprising the SPV's memorandum and articles, minutes of shareholder and board meetings, management or administrative services agreement, physical office lease or registered agent explanation, projected dividend policy, feasibility study for the downstream subsidiary investment, tax residency certificate and the China-foreign double-tax treaty analysis, and annual audited financial statements of the WFOE.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident shareholder must effect an SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the WFOE's designated SAFE-registered foreign exchange capital account at a Tier-1 commercial bank. The remittance narrative must specify the purpose as capital contribution or investment in registered capital, using the standard inward remittance purpose declaration code relevant to foreign direct investment in China. The domestic receiving bank will verify that the amount matches the registered capital with the Market Regulation Administration and will file the transaction with SAFE. After receipt and conversion into RMB, a certified public accountant issues a capital verification report, which is required for further commercial-registration filings and for subsequent remittance of dividends. All settlement disbursements must be supported by underlying contracts, invoices, and board resolutions and must not violate the negative-list restrictions on capital account settlement funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the holding SPV and its downstream operating subsidiaries, outbound payments should be cleared through licensed domestic bank channels using SWIFT MT103 for direct cash transfers, commercial letters of credit (L/C) for documentary trade settlements, and documentary collections where the seller ships under a bill of lading and the bank handles documents through an advised collection. As the SPV is primarily passive and not itself a goods trader, the most relevant outbound flows are dividends and loan repayments to the foreign parent, which require audited profit calculations, tax withholding certificates, board minutes, and SAFE current-account payment declarations. Any trade-related payment executed by an underlying subsidiary must maintain matching customs declarations and invoice evidence to preserve the bank's allowed trade credit status.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/USD and RMB/HKD forward contracts entered into for real existing current-account or capital-account exposures with a SAFE-licensed bank
FX swaps between spot and forward contracts for temporary RMB liquidity conversion when the WFOE has verified underlying foreign-currency receipts or obligations

Cross-currency interest rate swaps in RMB and USD where the notional amount is supported by the WFOE's actual borrowings or intercompany loans and where the bank confirms SAFE derivative qualification

Offshore non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts concluded only by the foreign parent or an offshore treasury center in Hong Kong or another acceptable jurisdiction, not by the onshore WFOE, because onshore enterprises are not permitted speculative NDF transactions without real physical settlement eligibility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report including Foreign Investment Information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; data automatically shared with the Ministry of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 January through 30 June of the year following each fiscal year ended 31 December; no anniversary extension for foreign-invested enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file on time triggers placement on the SAMR enterprises operating abnormally list with public disclosure; after three consecutive years of non-rectification the entity is moved to the serious illegal and untrustworthy list, restrictions are imposed on alteration and deregistration, and SAMR may eventually administratively revoke the business license. False or concealed foreign investment information is additionally sanctionable under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures, exposing the entity to correction orders and administrative fines up to RMB 300,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Reconciliation Return and Audited Financial Statement Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local office of the State Taxation Administration (STA) where the WFOE is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following each calendar year; quarterly prepayments of corporate income tax are due within 15 days after each quarter-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment gives rise to a 0.05% per day surcharge on the unpaid tax; failure to file the annual return attracts a fine up to RMB 2,000 (RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 in serious cases); underreporting or evasion can attract 50% to 500% of the additional tax. Persistent non-filing allows the tax authority to freeze and attach assets, cancel the tax registration, and obstruct all corporate changes and deregistration; it does not automatically strike off the company but makes administrative strike-off inevitable in enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit of Financial Statements and Shareholder Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders meeting and board of shareholders; audit report issued by a PRC-licensed CPA firm and required to be available for SAMR and STA inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit fieldwork is performed after 31 December and the signed audit report must be completed and formally approved before the 30 June annual report filing deadline in the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No audit report by the filing deadline means the SAMR annual report cannot be truthfully completed; the company is exposed to the abnormal operations list, administrative fines for false annual information, and the issue of qualified or adverse audit opinions by the independent CPA firm; habitual non-compliance provides grounds for administrative revocation of the registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner and Actual Controller Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation via the annual report; records held on-site for PBOC and AML supervisory inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually embedded in the 1 January to 30 June enterprise annual report; any transfer of direct or ultimate ownership, actual controller change, or equity pledge must be filed with SAMR within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A 30-day missed shareholding or UBO report creates a defective registration that can invalidate third-party reliance protections and triggers penalties for untruthful reporting; prolonged omission is treated by SAMR as a serious compliance breach and can lead to restrictions on share transfers and ultimately administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold is available to exempt a PRC WFOE from annual audit. Every WFOE, including a pure equity holding SPV with no operating revenue, is legally required to appoint a PRC-registered accounting firm to audit its annual financial statements. The applicable threshold is therefore zero: total assets of USD 0 or more, annual turnover of USD 0 or more, and headcount of 0 or more all remain captured. Separate mandatory audit triggers also apply if the entity is part of a listed group, has state-owned investors, engages in financial or insurance activities, applies for external debt or financing requiring audited statements, or is randomly selected by SAMR or STA for compliance inspection in the course of annual report reconciliation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE, substantially converged with IFRS); consolidated investment structures should additionally apply IFRS or the ultimate parent country GAAP only for foreign consolidation purposes. PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law adjustments are then reflected in the corporate income tax return. Small-enterprise SME accounting concessions available under the PRC Small Enterprise Accounting Standards are not permitted to replace the full audit requirement for a WFOE used as an equity holding SPV.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual UBO confirmation is not a standalone license filing: the WFOE identifies each ultimate beneficial owner and each actual controller in the enterprise annual report by 30 June. In addition, any direct share transfer, indirect ultimate ownership change, change of actual controller, or transfer or pledge of equity interest must be reported to SAMR within 30 days from the effective date of the change. The company secretary must update the on-site ownership register, director register, charge register, and minute book at the same time, and the updated registers must remain available for PBOC anti-money-laundering examinations and SAMR or STA audits.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 to USD 2,000 per annum for a registered address, licensed agency services, and corporate secretarial support in Tier-1 and Tier-2 Chinese cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per annum for an independent audit of a WFOE pure-equity holding SPV with minimal transactions, exclusive of subsidiary consolidation work.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to a passive equity-holding WFOE. A 15% reduced Enterprise Income Tax rate is available only to qualifying High and New Technology Enterprises, to qualifying encouraged industries in Western Development regions, or to qualifying free-trade-zone encouraged activities; in every case the SPV must actually conduct the corresponding substantive business. R&D super-deduction and patent-box style incentives are unavailable to a pure equity holding SPV.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000, the A-class Annual Corporate Income Tax Return, together with supplementary schedules A105030 and A107014, filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Taxation portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual with mandatory quarterly prepayment filings.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly prepayment returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual CIT return and final settlement must be filed on or before May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1: Revenue from principal operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from sales, services, or commercial activities, excluding investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure equity holding SPV, this line must be zero unless a chargeable service is actually performed. Dividends received from Chinese resident subsidiaries must not be reported here; they are tax-exempt income and are recorded through the adjustment schedule, not as operating revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2: Cost of principal operations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to the principal operating revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Normally zero for a passive HoldCo. Any intercompany management fee paid to the foreign parent must be supported by real services, documentary evidence, and arm's length pricing; otherwise it is disallowed and treated as disguised profit repatriation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3: Selling, administrative and financial expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses, general administration expenses, and financing charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recharged group costs from abroad require valid contracts, proof of benefit, and Chinese-source withholding on cross-border service payments. If the SPV has no staff or local substance, these deductions are prime targets for special tax adjustment and are often fully recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4: Operating profit or loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue less costs, expenses, and period charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE receives foreign-source dividends, such dividends flow into total profit and are adjusted separately; they are not eligible for the domestic dividend exemption. Do not mix foreign-source dividends with exempt Chinese-source subsidiary dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items outside normal operations, including equity transfer gains, subsidies, fines, and foreign exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gain on disposal of a downstream Chinese subsidiary is taxable at 25%. Understatement or delayed recognition of equity transfer gain is a fatal red flag that triggers transfer pricing review, GAAR recharacterization, and potential criminal tax fraud exposure.

This is the starting point for CIT computation. All adjustments, including tax-exempt dividend exclusion, add-backs of excessive intercompany charges, and GAAR adjustments, are made in the adjustment lines below Box 6, not by manipulating this accounting profit figure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying exempt income, chiefly resident-to-resident dividend income under Article 26 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To claim the exemption for dividends from a Chinese resident subsidiary, maintain board resolutions, share registers, bank receipts, and proof that listed-share investments were continuously held for at least 12 months. Dividends from listed shares held less than 12 months must be recognized as taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit after statutory and special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use this line to confirm that all transfer pricing adjustments and treaty-relevant recharacterizations have been reflected. Non-resident withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties is not reported in the corporate CIT return but in the separate non-resident enterprise withholding tax filing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fine of RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 under Article 62 of the Tax Administration Law. Late payment accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax under Article 32. Tax evasion under Article 63 attracts recovery of the evaded tax plus a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount. Criminal fraud under Article 201 of the Criminal Law triggers liability where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax due, and can lead to imprisonment of up to 7 years. Serious tax dishonesty blacklisting also imposes travel bans and personal credit restrictions on responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident immediate shareholder must claim treaty relief before the remittance date through the e-taxation portal. The mandatory protocol requires submission of: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate of the foreign shareholder issued by the competent foreign tax authority; (ii) a beneficial ownership substantiation package showing substance, not just formal legal ownership; (iii) direct shareholding evidence satisfying the treaty ownership threshold, such as a 25% direct capital holding for the reduced PRC-Hong Kong DTA rate; (iv) board resolutions and dividend distribution documentation; and (v) completed non-resident contract filing and withholding return forms. The Chinese paying entity must withhold statutory 10% in the absence of an approved treaty reduction, with the difference refundable on application after receipt of the TRC and beneficial ownership evidence. Failing substantive ownership or control may trigger denial of treaty benefits and retroactive interest.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties and interest is also 10%. Under an applicable bilateral double tax treaty, rates may be reduced; for example, under the China-Hong Kong DTA the treaty rate is typically 7% for both interest and royalties, while dividends are reduced to 5% where the beneficial owner is a company that directly holds at least 25% of the payer's capital. Treaty relief requires the same Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership analysis, and source-payment documentation. Recharacterization as a hidden dividend or conduit payment can raise the effective WHT to the full 10% on top of additional CIT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 20,000,000 for annual related-party tangible-asset transactions; RMB 10,000,000 for annual related-party intangible-asset transfers; RMB 10,000,000 for annual related-party financial-asset transfers; and other thresholds under SAT Announcement [2016] No. 42. Master File preparation may also apply where group-wide related-party turnover exceeds RMB 1,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply British-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the substance principle is embedded in the General Anti-Avoidance Rule under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and in the Chinese beneficial ownership doctrine. A pure equity holding SPV must demonstrate actual management decision-making, board meetings in China, real employees, physical or shared office premises, independently controlled bank accounts, and core income-generating activities (CIGA) in China. Absent such substance, the SPV may be recharacterized as a conduit, treaty benefits will be denied, underpaying income will be re-assessed at 25% CIT, and further deemed remittances may be subject to 10% WHT, plus surcharges, penalties, and blacklisting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting equity transfer gains from the disposal of a PRC subsidiary, reporting artificial zero revenue, or classifying foreign-source dividends as tax-exempt domestic dividends without satisfying the 12-month holding or Chinese-resident payer conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Law Article 63: recovery of the evaded tax, daily late-payment surcharge, and a fine of 50% to 500% of the underpaid amount. Criminal Law Article 201: where evasion exceeds RMB 100,000 and 10% of the tax due, the responsible person can receive imprisonment of up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil can be pierced where the director signed a false return and controlled the concealment; the director then bears joint and several civil liability for the State's tax loss. The director may be placed on the Serious Tax Dishonesty Blacklist, triggering a travel ban, denial of exit at the border, prohibition on serving as a legal representative elsewhere, and exposure to criminal imprisonment for a coordinated fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive DTA and conduit structures lacking economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Chinese dividends through a Hong Kong or other shell intermediate that has no real employees, no local management, no substantive decision-making, and no income-generating activities, then claiming a 5% or otherwise reduced treaty dividend withholding rate solely to avoid the statutory 10% WHT while control remains with the ultimate parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Enterprise Income Tax Law Article 47 and the SAT's anti-avoidance rules: the tax authority may recharacterize the conduit, deny treaty benefits, reassess 25% CIT on the underlying profits, impose 10% WHT on deemed distributions, and charge interest for late payment. If the concealment is fraudulent, Article 63 of the Tax Administration Law may additionally impose a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax shortfall, and GAAR reassessment can extend 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign beneficial ownership declarations while knowing the company is a conduit can be personally liable for the additionally assessed tax, interest, and penalties. The courts may disregard the corporate entity and attach personal assets of the directors. A permanent exit ban and blacklisting apply to directors of companies found to be instruments of tax fraud, and the forging or fraudulent use of treaty-related certificates could lead to criminal imprisonment of up to 7 years under criminal fraud provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold non-resident income tax on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making an outward wire transfer to the foreign parent for dividends, intercompany debt interest, or royalty payments without withholding at the statutory 10% rate, without filing the non-resident enterprise withholding tax return, and without documenting the applicable treaty reduction before remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Law Article 69 requires the Chinese resident payer to withhold and remit the tax; failure to do so triggers a fine of 50% to 300% of the un-withheld amount and the withholding agent remains liable for any uncollected tax. Late daily surcharge of 0.05% accrues from the statutory due date, and false or omitted declarations can cross criminal fraud thresholds under Article 201 of the Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize outbound dividend, interest, or royalty remittances without proper withholding expose the company to tax losses for which they can be held civilly liable. Once the company is blacklisted under the joint enforcement memorandum, the responsible director becomes subject to a travel ban and exit control, cannot open new enterprises, and may face personal confiscation of assets. Where the absence of withholding is part of a larger scheme to strip profits and evade tax, the director is also exposed to personal criminal prosecution and imprisonment.
